evidence streams remain isolated. Preserve
publication and release ordering. Inspect the configured queue mode and
cancellation semantics; do not assume workflow dispatch order is execution order.
Concurrency groups do not supply merge-candidate validation. Follow GitHub's
[concurrency semantics](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-when-workflows-run/control-workflow-concurrency)
and the project's [merge-check rules](testing-feedback-loop.md#merge-queues-and-required-merge-checks).

## Fix instability at the owning boundary

Classify a failure before changing its budget: product regression, fixture race,
resource exhaustion, dependency/service failure or unavailable infrastructure.
Retain the failing source and attempt, first error, relevant trace and measured
phase. A passing rerun is diagnostic information, not a root-cause explanation.
Playwright explicitly [classifies a retry pass as flaky](https://playwright.dev/docs/test-retries);
keep first-attempt and retry outcomes distinct.

Synchronize with observable readiness and the exact operation being tested.
Register observers before triggering transient events; correlate signals with
request identity, immutable control state and the lifetime of the actual task.
Historical logs or a previously authenticated request do not prove that a live
request has entered the required phase. Keep cancellation, task joining and
cleanup correct on success, failure and panic.
Give pre-arm setup and the measured admission separate bounded phases; an
independent watchdog must not release a test barrier merely because unrelated
preparation consumed its observation window. Keep the owning API's pending/error
distinction in bounded observers. The
[failure-evidence rules](ai-coding-reliability.md#r10-evidence-that-exercises-the-failure)
identify the owning retirement-observer regression.
When key ordering determines the scenario, use deterministic noncolliding fixture
identities and check actual signed keys or cursors; random IDs can exercise only
the easier path. Preserve real signing, publication and receipt assertions.
Keep commit, completed publication and recipient installation distinct. A
post-timeout snapshot can block behind the publisher and cannot prove its state
existed before the cutoff; record phases at the actual work owner.
Use the owning register-before-check notification protocol for durable status;
polling an in-memory flag can still compete with the work that must publish it.
Match a fixture's executor to its requirement: preserve single-thread tests when
responsiveness is the subject, and keep independent protocol/persistence workers
for other production-runtime scenarios. Join admitted work before deleting data.
Classify fixture gates from the current decision owner's state, not a trace flag
that also describes another phase. Do not sample a later observer projection to
decide whether to capture a one-shot event; observe that evidence before releasing
the captured task and retain its exact operation and child identity.

Separate expensive fixture preparation from the operation's measured window when
preparation is outside the requirement. Continue using the real signing,
persistence, transport or UI owner when it is part of the assertion. Preserve
production deadlines and real lifecycle coverage where those are the subject of
the test; changing the clock or injecting state cannot silently remove them.
A held real socket still consumes its production timeout while a fixture waits.
Finish unrelated cold preparation before dispatching that read, using a scoped
owned barrier before I/O where necessary. Do not pause a post-send hook to conceal
the network timeout. Consolidate repeated readiness polls into that preparation
owner; retain exact live-task and measured-operation assertions at admission.

Batch unobserved durable fixture construction through an existing validated
transaction seam when individual commit boundaries are outside the requirement.
Retain every signed event, per-event validation and index update, a completed
durable commit before observation, exact corpus assertions and the original
measured operation. Never batch away the transaction boundaries under test.
Commit CLI fixture infrastructure to its private baseline before introducing the
intended source change; unrelated copied tools must not inflate changed-file
validation or consume the assertion's watchdog.

Lifecycle regressions should exercise the real supervisor and child processes
without making unrelated host tool startup part of their success condition. Full-host
network fixtures must use the existing independent device runtime owner, retain
the original offline/online cuts and observation budgets, and join actual work
before profile reuse on success and failure. A timer sharing a synchronously
stalled reactor provides no independent watchdog; isolate device scheduling
rather than extending timeouts or assigning one shared reactor more workers.
Include actual sender recovery and bound advertised listeners, not only recipient
loops and a best-effort send. Keep the genuine held-worker delivery control
alongside reconnect acceptance. [Reactor ownership](ai-coding-reliability.md#r02-thread-and-scheduler-progress)
also explains why direct observer work remains a watchdog limitation. Local
fixture success does not establish a historical lock cause or native qualification.
When tool identity is outside the assertion, reuse the existing
[tool-version fixture](../scripts/diagnostics/test-fixtures/tool-versions.mjs)
and verify that its probes were actually consumed. Keep the real command,
failure, cancellation and receipt assertions and their existing watchdogs.
When adding a local check, inspect subprocess fixtures that invoke its owner.
Supply unrelated external tools through private, observed fixture dependencies;
do not depend on developer-installed tools or add scanner setup to every runner
just to exercise scheduling. Keep real scanner acceptance in its existing job.
Exercise interrupted log finalization as well as child retirement through the
existing [process-owner controls](ai-coding-reliability.md#r03-actual-work-owns-its-lifetime).
Compare nested budgets before adding an outer subprocess timeout: several valid
inner probes can exhaust it before the behavior under test starts. A passing PR
run cannot qualify an unbounded environmental dependency for later main runs.
Do not use a fixed sleep to infer that background synchronization has happened.
Bind negative assertions to an actual post-change operation: for deletion replay,
prove the erased record was offered again and all pages were applied before
checking that it remains absent. A successful page, unchanged-digest response or
unrelated worker notification does not prove a complete replay. Keep deadlines
as failure bounds, and retain ownership and joins for admitted work on timeout.
Request that work through its existing coordinator and observe its publication
revision and terminal completion. A second hand-driven page loop can race the
normal worker and bypass its serialization, recovery and cancellation contract.
Capture immutable precondition evidence before admitting an operation that can
invalidate it. Published projections may legitimately become pending during a
commit; a post-admission read cannot prove the operation's initial role. Wait on
the existing preparation owner within the original setup deadline and fail
unexpected errors instead of retrying the whole operation.
Give counterfactual source copies their own Cargo target directory. Relative
package paths can collide across copies and reuse a mutated test executable;
the canonical candidate must never consume a negative control's build output.
Asynchronous progress notifications are observations, not readiness barriers. Cancellation
fixtures must bind readiness to still-live owned work after the required real
materialization, then assert its retirement before later admission or cleanup;
a bounded fallback may fail missing readiness but cannot manufacture a pass.

Executable fixtures must own an independent copied image, not a hard link to
the running test harness. Assert file identity before launch. After verified
process retirement, use the shared bounded filesystem cleanup helper; persistent
locks must still fail. Keep the Windows held-image failure and release controls
in `release-reuse.test.mjs`; cleanup retries never retry the test assertion or
substitute for process retirement.

Git-path and mode controls should construct Git objects when the host cannot
represent the input faithfully. Assert the actual delta and mode before checking
rejection; an empty change rejected for another reason is not a valid negative
control. Keep these cases on every platform instead of skipping them.

Browser commands use the existing process owner with a deadline inside the total
job budget, reserving time for joined cleanup and evidence upload. Keep streamed
logs and append-only active/completed-case progress when final reports cannot be
written. Timeout or uncertain cleanup remains a failure. Preserve verified closure of owned work as a diagnostic separately from the
actual child outcome: Windows
intentionally terminates even an empty job to close descendant admission.
On POSIX, verify the framework's independently grouped web server as well as the
CLI group. Use its supported graceful interruption protocol; a missing teardown
acknowledgment means cleanup remains unverified. Bind lifecycle markers to the
current invocation so old evidence cannot prove a later process stopped.
Do not await output-pipe closure indefinitely after the command leader exits.

rejected, rather than only matching the generated call text. Ownership checks and
real desktop acceptance remain separate from generator/compilation checks.

## Review the change and prevent renewed drift

Follow the existing validation stages; do not invent a parallel completion
process. For changes affecting CI behavior or recurring cost, include the
following in the normal [alignment review](maintenance-checklist.md#review-and-follow-up-procedure):

- The acceptance boundary and retained owner, including consumers affected by
  deletion, merging, selection or schedule changes.
- The measured bottleneck, comparable before/after scope and remaining unknowns;
  distinguish observed latency, resource cost and reliability.
- Executed validation and source identity, with inventory/provenance checks or
  regression controls appropriate to the changed mechanism.
- Remaining hosted, cross-platform, native or release evidence and the owner of
  any follow-up. Do not claim candidate acceptance from local or older results.

Workflow, runner and tool upgrades can change CLI semantics, report formats,
selectors and archive compatibility. Validate affected real tool invocations and
failure paths through the existing diagnostic owners; YAML parsing or unit mocks
alone do not establish the behavior of the installed tool.

when the ordinary and coverage commands select the same inventory and platform
branches use explicit mocks. Verify that inventory with the actual runner before
removing duplicate OS executions. Retain real browser/native matrices and native
diagnostic fixtures; mocked platform branches do not supply those contracts.
Keep Node/filesystem portability requirements in their owning diagnostics rather
than duplicating the entire frontend unit suite incidentally.

Keep platform-exclusive probes in the required native producer that can execute
them. Universal local selections must not include a file whose entire suite is

After pushing, observe the actual hosted candidate until the relevant jobs finish.
Compare before and after setup time, test time, required-check latency and runner

changes, then make another measured pass when evidence identifies remaining waste.

an end-to-end speedup. Keep the candidate reviewable and continue in a clean
worktree when unrelated local edits prevent publication; do not discard those
edits or treat them as a reason to stop the optimization.

Revisit timing and failure evidence when a gate becomes slower, starts rerunning,
gains another platform/dependency, or repeatedly exceeds its expected budget.
During existing maintenance reviews, inspect slow cases, duplicated setup,
shard imbalance, cache churn and abandoned temporary exceptions. Retire obsolete
work with its consumers and selectors rather than accumulating permanent layers.

Keep this review proportional: a documentation-only change needs applicable
formatting, links and structural checks, not a new build benchmark. Rules should
be enforceable through existing contracts and diagnostics where practical;

# AI coding reliability guide

Use this guide before implementing or reviewing a change, especially a bug fix,
refactor, merge resolution or optimization. Its purpose is to turn recurring
failure modes into concrete design questions and executable checks. Compiling,
adding a timeout or passing a happy-path test does not establish reliability.

This guide owns the cross-cutting review method and reusable failure patterns.
[Module ownership](module-boundaries.md) owns implementation boundaries;
[architecture](ARCHITECTURE.md), [network contracts](network-design-reference.md)
and feature guides own behavior and resource limits. The
[testing workflow](testing-feedback-loop.md) owns commands, selection and gates.
Link to those owners instead of copying their changing contracts here. When code
and a contract disagree, resolve the intended behavior rather than documenting
the regression as the new rule.

## Use on every change

1. **Locate the owner and consumers.** Read the owning implementation, callers,
   existing tests and relevant guide before adding another helper or state owner.
   Include callbacks, IPC handlers, retries, startup, shutdown and recovery paths;
   an import graph alone cannot reveal all consumers.
2. **State the invariant and select risks.** Describe what must remain true on
   success, failure, cancellation and replacement. Use the table below to select
   applicable rules. A small diff can change lock order or lifetime semantics.
3. **Trace the failure path before editing.** For concurrency work, sketch who
   owns each lock, permit, task and mutable state; what it waits for; and who
   releases it. For a reproducible bug, construct a focused failing regression.
   Record unresolved hypotheses as hypotheses, not confirmed defects.
4. **Implement at the existing boundary.** Preserve authority, durable acceptance,
   compatibility and resource budgets. Recheck invariants after moving work
   outside a guard. Evaluate the proposed fix for new races and deadlocks too.
5. **Verify the changed boundary and report evidence.** Run affected checks and
   required boundary scenarios under the testing workflow. Explain results,
   exclusions and unresolved evidence. Update this guide when the defect exposes
   a reusable failure pattern; follow the maintenance procedure below.

Keep the risk explanation proportional to the change. A documentation edit does
not require a new concurrency test. A changed async callback does require a
lifetime review even when the diff is one line. Put task-specific reasoning and
results in the PR or ignored local evidence, not a new permanent report.

Cross-cutting idle budgets, demand-driven work and accumulation rules belong to
[performance requirements](performance-requirements.md). Apply them alongside the
correctness rules below; a smaller resource chart does not prove preserved recovery.

## Select rules by the changed boundary

| Change or symptom                                                        | Read at least                                                                                                                                         |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Locks, callbacks, synchronous dispatch, UI freezes                       | [R01](#r01-lock-order-and-reentrant-calls), [R02](#r02-thread-and-scheduler-progress), [R10](#r10-evidence-that-exercises-the-failure)                |
| Background work, native providers, logout, shutdown or cancellation      | [R02](#r02-thread-and-scheduler-progress), [R03](#r03-actual-work-owns-its-lifetime), [R06](#r06-exact-authority-and-stale-completions)               |
| Network requests, retries, polling, queues or batches                    | [R03](#r03-actual-work-owns-its-lifetime), [R04](#r04-deadlines-cover-the-whole-operation), [R05](#r05-bounded-work-must-also-make-progress)          |
| React effects, IPC reads, dialogs, optimistic updates or mutation status | [R06](#r06-exact-authority-and-stale-completions), [R07](#r07-observation-is-not-mutation-ownership), [R10](#r10-evidence-that-exercises-the-failure) |
| Storage, settings, imports, deletion or recovery                         | [R06](#r06-exact-authority-and-stale-completions), [R08](#r08-durable-state-and-failure-semantics), [R09](#r09-bound-input-and-resource-use)          |
| IPC/API inputs, files, media or protocol changes                         | [R06](#r06-exact-authority-and-stale-completions), [R08](#r08-durable-state-and-failure-semantics), [R09](#r09-bound-input-and-resource-use)          |
| Merge resolution, shared helper or dependency changes                    | Revisit the affected callers and all applicable rules; a clean textual merge does not establish compatible ownership or semantics.                    |

These are starting points, not permission to ignore another reachable boundary.
Do not add a global lock, retry loop, timeout or shared abstraction solely to make
the local symptom disappear.

A frozen UI may result from a lock cycle, blocked event thread, starvation, lost
wakeup, unbounded work or stale loading state. Identify the mechanism and the
missing progress condition before selecting a fix; these need different evidence.

## R01: Lock order and reentrant calls

**Failure pattern:** one path takes A then B while another takes B then A; or a
helper/callback reacquires a nonrecursive lock its caller already holds. The
second case can deadlock on a single thread. Nested reads also need review when
a queued writer can prevent a new read from completing.

Trace actual acquisition order through callees, authorization callbacks,
destructors and error cleanup. Include main-thread dispatch and task joins as
wait dependencies, not just mutexes. A typical UI cycle is:

```text
background task: holds session guard -> waits for main-thread callback
main thread:     handles UI event    -> waits for session guard
```

Use the owning module's order; do not invent one universal order for unrelated
subsystems. Make whether a helper acquires a guard or requires one explicit.
Account archive snapshots, history projections and delivery recovery share the
plaintext-sidecar order: sent, received, then received files. Recovery must not
hold received while waiting for sent: an archive has no delivery guard and can
otherwise hold sent while waiting for received. The real recovery regression
`recovery_does_not_hold_received_while_waiting_for_sent` in the
[recovery owner](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/delivery_runtime.rs) holds sent,
probes received at the actual acquisition boundary, then releases contention and
joins the worker before asserting replay and progress.
Archive revision snapshots must read and release device-sync policy before
acquiring plaintext sidecars. Attachment commit holds delivery and policy while
checking the live received-file card; an archive holding received files while
waiting for policy creates a cycle and can also block erasure behind delivery.
Keep archive-key revalidation after indexing and page selection so a changed
policy still invalidates the export. The regression belongs to the
[account archive owner](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/account_sync/archive.rs)
and must qualify progress while the competing policy/sidecar boundary is held,
then release and join both owners before asserting the outcome.
The same boundary applies to file-proof revisions: identity import holds the
proof store while validating received-file rows. Archive snapshots must read and
release proof metadata before taking sidecars, and retain proof revision in the
final archive-key validation. Its separate held-proof regression qualifies the
actual archive path; policy-only coverage does not establish this lock order.
Do not build a revision array from chained mutex temporaries: guards can survive
until the entire array statement ends. Snapshot each value in a completed
statement before acquiring the next metadata lock. The archive's held-identity
control must also prove suppression is free, preserving the identity-then-
suppression order used by file-row visibility checks.
Avoid invoking arbitrary callbacks while guarded. Where a commit callback must
run inside an authority guard, keep that contract narrow and inspect its complete
call chain. Queue presentation without retaining a guard needed by the UI;
validate captured authority when the queued callback executes.

Rust [temporary scopes](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/destructors.html#temporary-scopes)
can keep guards alive through the complete statement, including struct literals
and tuples. Read repeated owner scalars under one explicit short guard,
then release it before constructing a value that could acquire the owner again.
Check the actual temporary scope before declaring a cycle: each operand of a lazy
Boolean expression has its own temporary scope. An explicit short block can make
an observation boundary clearer without changing an already-released guard.

**Evidence:** exercise both competing paths and the real authorization variant.
An ordinary admission fixture does not cover a sensitive proof that itself locks
app state. Assert that the other operation progresses, not just that the first
eventually returns. See `checked_at_lock_revision` in
[runtime admission](../src-tauri/src/runtime_admission.rs), the verified-login
regression in [shared login tests](../src-tauri/src/shared_account_login/tests.rs),
and queued notification tests in [runtime state](../src-tauri/src/chat_commands/state.rs).

## R02: Thread and scheduler progress

**Failure pattern:** an `async` function performs blocking disk, crypto, OS-provider
or process work; a blocking worker retains a globally needed guard; or the parent
scheduler awaits optional work before polling unrelated ready operations.

Identify the executing thread and scheduling owner, not just the function's
signature. Move blocking work through the existing admitted worker boundary.
Inspect React render/effect/subscriber feedback loops and large synchronous data
transforms too; moving I/O off the UI thread does not bound those CPU costs.
Subscribe to status-only observations at the smallest presentation owner. A
parent chat subscription can rerender its virtualized message viewport for every
peer-check timestamp even when the rows are unchanged. The mounted
[conversation idle regression](../frontend/src/features/chat/ConversationViewIdle.test.ts)
requires live status updates without viewport renders, while new messages and
conversation replacement remain live.
Apply the same semantic boundary to native effects: the mounted
[chat shell regression](../frontend/src/features/chat/ChatAppIdle.test.ts) requires
unchanged notification context through peer freshness and ordering changes,
while real conversation/device-set changes, session replacement and unmount
retain publication and cleanup. Native revision admission still fences stale calls.
Prepare bulk data outside shared commit guards, then reacquire the required
guards and revalidate before atomic publication. Keep critical sections small
without splitting a transaction or permitting stale side effects. Replacing a
mutex with an async mutex alone does not repair ownership or lock order.

Evaluate authoritative cheap decisions before expensive fallback work. An exact
accepted identity binding or direct current policy grant must not first scan
unrelated history to establish an alternative grant. If policy can change,
recheck at the write owner; release its guard before obtaining missing fallback
evidence. The [privacy admission tests](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/privacy_runtime_tests.rs)
require real certified-sibling SessionReady while unrelated histories are held,
and exercise policy tightening with and without genuine shared-group authority.
Treat scheduling digests as storage work when they acquire a repository or
history guard. Account-channel and custody observations use the existing serial
repair worker and release its capacity before network work. The maintenance
regression `scheduling_input_waits_for_history_without_blocking_its_reactor`
holds real history while probing the observer's own reactor, then releases and
joins both owners before checking the unchanged digest. A separate full-host
SessionReady test retains the real network boundary and its original deadline.

Check that the UI event loop, accept loop and control scheduler can still make
progress while the worker is paused. Offloading a scan does not help other
branches of a scheduler if that scheduler still waits for the entire scan inside
one completion branch. Synchronous final persistence can still block; document
that boundary instead of claiming a timer can preempt it.

Trace guards inside a helper named `blocking`, not only the caller. A read-only
image decode must not hold the global session/app-lock guard throughout its CPU

runtime in a detached parent until its actual worker joins, checks one admission

publication. Its held-worker regression checks unrelated session progress and
that observer timeout does not release worker capacity or runtime ownership.

Branches of one `select!` share a task; adding runtime workers does not let a
blocked branch poll another branch of that same future. Independently scheduled
work must keep an explicit parent cancellation owner and retain the actual
child's retirement permit. The [inbound serving owner](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/serving.rs)

[account action tests](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/account_group/tests/message_action_reference.rs),

same independent host and retirement owner, including separate reactors for both
full-host participants and the synchronous history observer. The single-participant
connection-limit/retirement fixture likewise uses the production two-worker host;
retain its seven-slot saturation, original admission/retirement bounds and actual
socket closure checks, alongside the held-worker positive and single-thread
negative controls. This qualifies fixture capacity without attributing every
historical late admission to scheduler starvation. A source's synchronous durable append must not run on the receiver's
reactor. The growing-history regression in
[account sync tests](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/account_sync/selection_tests.rs)
holds the actual source writer until a receiver page imports, then measures
continuation progress separately from setup and checks advancing cursors.
Full-host file fixtures retain a separate two-worker reactor for each simulated
application. The [linked reconnect fixture](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/node_tests.rs)
also uses that owner at its original offline/online cuts and joins admitted work
before reopening a profile, on failure as well as success. This separates device
accept and maintenance loops; direct observer queries and public sends, including
caller-owned idle-expiry tasks, can still run on the observer reactor. A timer on
that reactor cannot bound a synchronous stall. Preserve the observation budget
and do not infer a particular deadlock or complete watchdog independence from an
unpolled timer alone. This includes the explicit account File result/retry rigs: use the
existing independent peer owner for source, requester, recipient and the launched
fresh sibling, keeping inactive retry phases and every byte/manifest assertion.
Release fault helpers before joining hosts, and preserve body failure after

holds both sibling workers after its durable copy completes and requires target
confirmation while they remain held; unrelated devices cannot share that stall.
The sender-restart control closes work admission, joins producers, clears pooled
sessions and drains admitted reception work before reopening the profile. A
recipient receipt certifies delivery while that cleanup may still own its lease.

**Evidence:** pause actual expensive work after admission and assert availability
of the unrelated guard or operation. Release the pause and verify the final data.
See the attachment preparation and document-scheduler regressions in
[account sync tests](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/account_sync/selection_tests.rs).

Reuse an immutable certificate binding through the owner that validated it on
admission and reopen. A hot membership query must not clone/sort the full roster
and reverify signatures per row/page. Keep exact account and exchange-key checks,
and retain current policy/revocation fences. The
[roster regressions](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/account_devices.rs) count
actual verifier calls through `Node::certified_sibling` while rejecting forged
admission/reopen records and substituted exchange keys.

Async discovery observers must use the existing owned asynchronous peer-cache
snapshot and preserve persistence errors. The synchronous desktop convenience
snapshot writes storage and converts errors to an empty roster; polling it can
block the observer's reactor or misreport failed persistence as discovery latency.
Native queries release the runtime slot before awaiting that owned work and
recheck the exact installed Node before publishing; a replaced or removed runtime
cannot supply the new session's peers. The [peer-query controls](../src-tauri/src/chat_commands/account.rs)
exercise real cache failure/recovery through the managed command and separately
hold its observer boundary to verify slot progress and stale-result rejection.
The [account-login fixture](../src-tauri/src/shared_account_login/tests.rs) retains
its single signed loopback probe and original deadline, and a real cache-path
failure must preserve the cache API's error chain rather than time out. This
control proves error visibility, not the cause of an earlier hosted timeout.

Sharing a read must not join unrelated latency dependencies. The roster owner
shares only peers and people; conditional group metadata runs outside session
and runtime-slot guards through participant-owned work. The held-metadata and
cancelled-observer controls in [owner commands](../src-tauri/src/owner_commands.rs)
require unrelated identity/peer progress and retirement to await the actual
worker. Frontend roster tickets belong to one invalidation, preserve original
evidence age and never carry a result into another runtime generation.

## R03: Actual work owns its lifetime

Keep concurrency capacity with the same actual owner as retirement admission.
Cancelling a scheduler must not release a serial maintenance slot while its
blocking worker or captures remain alive. Acquire only at top-level local-work
ent…6283 tokens truncated…rkers to the
current invocation so old evidence cannot prove a later process stopped.
Do not await output-pipe closure indefinitely after the command leader exits.
The existing process owner bounds draining after group retirement; a separately
grouped descendant retaining stdout or stderr must yield a failed structured
result with unverified cleanup and a quarantined lease. Closing owned read ends
does not prove the escaped process stopped. Keep real natural-exit, cancellation
and no-success-receipt controls rather than signalling unknown process groups.
Authorize PID cleanup only from a complete private acknowledgment, not a numeric
prefix in a stdout chunk. Stream reads do not preserve message boundaries; a
failed readiness publication must retire the child through its creation owner.
Actual CLI regression fixtures need private output directories as well as private
source directories; parallel Playwright commands otherwise delete one another's
traces and manufacture failures. Missing hosted logs do not identify a slow case.
Local-only evidence fixtures must explicitly isolate and restore inherited CI
flags, and separately assert that real CI cannot reuse local acceptance evidence.
Health captures its absolute budget before setup and uses the existing stage
owner to stop diagnostics before the job watchdog. Preserve its structured result,
execution log and bounded Node lifecycle records, including the active file/case,
through the always-upload path. Prove interruption and joined cleanup with a real
parked command. Missing hosted logs require better evidence, not a guessed fix.
Native release stdout may omit application warnings. After actual child retirement,
the existing native capture owner retains bounded, redacted private application
file-log tails in the uploaded evidence. Prefer the current log within bounded
selection, reject linked/nonregular paths, close handles and report missing or
unreadable diagnostics without replacing the original failure. Do not collect
these logs through the IPC channel whose responsiveness is under investigation.
`native-capture.test.mjs` owns confinement, quotas, cutoff redaction and retirement
controls; file-log presence does not establish a backend failure cause.
Cancellation during preparation still needs a failed structured result. Only the
command owner can attest that admission never happened; failures after that
boundary must retain uncertain cleanup rather than manufacture a no-work result.

The [fixture timing guidance](testing-feedback-loop.md#cold-fixture-preparation-versus-measured-progress)
owns concrete examples and permitted boundaries.

Prefer bounded condition waits and meaningful failure diagnostics. Browser
actions should use [Playwright actionability and retrying assertions](https://playwright.dev/docs/actionability)
where applicable; application readiness may still need its own signal. Arbitrary
sleeps, broader timeouts, blanket retries and weaker assertions need evidence;
they are not default repairs for an unexplained failure. If a narrowly scoped
infrastructure retry is justified, keep its limit, original failure and outcomes
visible, and ensure repeating the operation is safe. Test retries still obey the
owning suite policy.

Keep asynchronous fixture discovery observations on the existing owned async
peer-cache API. A synchronous convenience snapshot can perform disk writes and
hide a cache failure behind an empty roster. The account-login fixture retains
one signed probe and its original five-second discovery budget, while a real
cache-path failure must surface the cache API's error chain before that deadline.
Retain the core cache writer's cancellation/profile-lease controls. A successful
rerun does not identify the mechanism of a previous missing-peer timeout.
A cached peer can already satisfy the identity predicate while a newly sent
query remains outstanding. The [restart fixture](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/runtime_privacy_tests.rs)
also requires a response to a nonce issued by that invocation, from its exact
endpoint, with the actually accepted device/account binding. Keep the original
whole observation deadline, probe cadence and count; subsequent cooldown starts
after witnessed completion. Real warm-cache/retired-target and restart controls
must reject the cached-only shortcut. Test-only packet witnesses are opt-in,
instance-owned and bounded, expose omissions, avoid disabled formatting work and
retire real listener tasks. They add evidence, not network authority or a claimed
explanation of unobserved packet loss.

Explicit-endpoint discovery fixtures retire the named broadcast, scan and rejoin
tasks through their existing participant owner while retaining the real UDP
listener, public policy, certificates, TCP and delivery work. On their current-thread
runtime, qualify retirement before the producers' first poll with per-instance
entry counts and three actual joins; the control must detect normal ambient
startup. Abort all selected tasks before awaiting any, join every handle and
retain failures until cleanup completes. Production still launches all four
discovery tasks. This isolates a fixture's environment-dependent traffic; it does
not establish an empty OS interface inventory or resolve production socket pressure.

When a UI action moves into a menu, update the existing shared interaction helper
and its callers before publication. Exercise the real entry point; retain
functional, permission, focus and geometry assertions at the toolbar or popup
boundary they describe. The
[composer attachment helper](../frontend/e2e/helpers/session.ts) owns that shared
interaction; forced visibility and dropped assertions do not qualify the new flow.

Keep each observation inside a polling assertion nonwaiting when the assertion
already owns readiness. A locator operation can wait for a virtualized row and
consume the entire outer budget without producing one decode or geometry sample.
Inspect the trace to distinguish missing samples from unequal values; use one
browser-side DOM snapshot, treating an absent row as pending. Establish visible
fixture preparation before releasing held media bytes and starting decode checks.
Preserve exact geometry and cache assertions, and exercise the absent-row control
with a snapshot-only observer rather than extending the deadline. The media-scroll
remount regression owns this case. Run independent adversarial sampler controls
after the cache-remount journey, so they cannot consume its retention window.
The [group reading-anchor fixture](../frontend/e2e/group-reception.spec.ts) uses
the same nonwaiting page snapshot for its initial visible row. Capture its exact
identity and offset together; retain the outer poll budget and all subsequent
anchor, focus, unread and navigation assertions. A late successful observation
does not establish a missing-row defect or identify the source of driver latency.
Initial history preparation uses a browser-local observer for exact row identity,
text and visible geometry within the caller's original remaining budget. Keep
mutation checks immediate and a deduplicated frame fallback; absent/hidden rows
must fail and queued recovery must clean up even with frames held. Check the
monotonic deadline before and after sampling so delayed callbacks cannot accept
a late state. Preserve every later live/read, scroll and focus assertion.

The [memory guardrail](../frontend/e2e/memory.spec.ts) retains its seeded history,
25 complete conversation rounds, original watchdog and rendered-bubble ceiling.
Exercise a trusted pointer round, then activate the same DOM buttons through one
browser-side journey for repeated churn, with visible rows, exact active
destinations and loaded-history assertions after every activation. Retire each
bounded readiness observer's timer and callback. This isolates store/list
replacement from repeated driver round trips without invoking a store action
directly; the repeated phase does not qualify trusted-input latency. Preserve
the final pointer navigation and DOM bound; a deliberate extra-bubble control
must still fail. This fixture does not measure pointer latency or prove the cause
of hosted driver stalls.
Its [observer](../frontend/e2e/helpers/conversation-churn.ts) checks DOM commits
without waiting for an animation frame, retaining the frame fallback for CSS-only
readiness. A held-frame browser control must cover the original readiness timeout,
observer/frame cleanup and recovery. Retained trace timing is bounded per completed
activation; it does not qualify a late assertion after the whole-test deadline.
The owning browser selector includes both the scenario and its helper.

For a reproducible race or timeout fix, use a regression or negative control that
fails for the original mechanism and passes with the repair. Confirm that the
intended case actually ran. Preserve existing coverage while investigating; any
temporary quarantine needs an explicit owner, reason, tracking issue and removal
condition under the existing gate policy.

## Reject incomplete discovery and generated-policy drift

Successful test execution requires successful, complete input discovery.
`scripts/ci/fuzz-targets.py` compares the discovered cargo-fuzz list with the actual
manifest-owned target inventory before running anything. Failed enumeration, an
empty list, duplicates, omissions or unknown targets fail the job, as do individual
target failures. Keep this assertion at the execution owner; shell loop command
substitution alone does not propagate discovery failure under `set -e`.

`scripts/ci/glib-migration.py` evaluates every resolved glib branch, rather than
treating a newer parallel branch as proof that an older stack was removed. Its
migration claim conservatively requires stable 0.20 or newer throughout; absent
glib and mixed old/new trees do not establish migration. The
[RustSec advisory](https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2024-0429.html) owns the
security version ranges; the watcher retains native build/test and reviewed-PR
requirements before changing dependencies.

Generated native input probes share one accepted-key/extended-flag metadata owner
between WebDriver mapping and emitted C# policy. Regressions must check that every
emitted key is accepted with the correct flags and unsupported keys remain
rejected, rather than only matching the generated call text. Ownership checks and
real desktop acceptance remain separate from generator/compilation checks.

## Review the change and prevent renewed drift

Follow the existing validation stages; do not invent a parallel completion
process. For changes affecting CI behavior or recurring cost, include the
following in the normal [alignment review](maintenance-checklist.md#review-and-follow-up-procedure):

- The acceptance boundary and retained owner, including consumers affected by
  deletion, merging, selection or schedule changes.
- The measured bottleneck, comparable before/after scope and remaining unknowns;
  distinguish observed latency, resource cost and reliability.
- Executed validation and source identity, with inventory/provenance checks or
  regression controls appropriate to the changed mechanism.
- Remaining hosted, cross-platform, native or release evidence and the owner of
  any follow-up. Do not claim candidate acceptance from local or older results.

Workflow, runner and tool upgrades can change CLI semantics, report formats,
selectors and archive compatibility. Validate affected real tool invocations and
failure paths through the existing diagnostic owners; YAML parsing or unit mocks
alone do not establish the behavior of the installed tool.

Consolidate frontend unit execution through the complete Linux coverage owner
when the ordinary and coverage commands select the same inventory and platform
branches use explicit mocks. Verify that inventory with the actual runner before
removing duplicate OS executions. Retain real browser/native matrices and native
diagnostic fixtures; mocked platform branches do not supply those contracts.
Keep Node/filesystem portability requirements in their owning diagnostics rather
than duplicating the entire frontend unit suite incidentally.

Keep platform-exclusive probes in the required native producer that can execute
them. Universal local selections must not include a file whose entire suite is
skipped on other hosts; preserve the nonempty-test guard and explicit native
escalation instead. Keep workflow wiring assertions in the cheap CI policy
owner, separate from the underlying tool's filesystem/compiler regressions.
Environment-specific cases must also distinguish unsupported local environments
from broken CI configuration. Skip only the new unsupported case, retain the
file's other checks, and declare its native escalation. A declared GitHub Linux
run must reach strict environment validation even when required image inputs are
missing; never turn that misconfiguration into a skip or fabricate hosted inputs.

After pushing, observe the actual hosted candidate until the relevant jobs finish.
Compare before and after setup time, test time, required-check latency and runner
minutes with sample sizes and cache conditions. Inspect first failures and queue
changes, then make another measured pass when evidence identifies remaining waste.
A pushed branch, a local green subset, or a faster isolated step does not establish
an end-to-end speedup. Keep the candidate reviewable and continue in a clean
worktree when unrelated local edits prevent publication; do not discard those
edits or treat them as a reason to stop the optimization.

Revisit timing and failure evidence when a gate becomes slower, starts rerunning,
gains another platform/dependency, or repeatedly exceeds its expected budget.
During existing maintenance reviews, inspect slow cases, duplicated setup,
shard imbalance, cache churn and abandoned temporary exceptions. Retire obsolete
work with its consumers and selectors rather than accumulating permanent layers.

Keep this review proportional: a documentation-only change needs applicable
formatting, links and structural checks, not a new build benchmark. Rules should
be enforceable through existing contracts and diagnostics where practical;
adding this guide does not create a scheduled job or another required check.

## Dependabot development acceptance

The existing exact-merge scope owner, `scripts/ci/docs-scope.mjs`, also admits
isolated npm dependency profiles for same-repository Dependabot bot PRs targeting
`dev`. Both manifests and lockfiles must already exist as regular files. Only
version changes to existing dependency entries qualify; scripts, overrides,
metadata, additions/removals, mixed paths, unmatched lockfile roots and changed
Tauri bindings retain full verification. Lockfile-only updates currently retain
full verification because their consumer boundary has not been qualified.

The `help` profile runs the public help/MCP tests, build and high-severity audit.
The `frontend` profile runs complete unit coverage, lint/types, production build,
built-JavaScript syntax checks, audit, Chromium theme/layout regressions and the
WebKit portable suite. The selected npm workflow independently checks its profile
against the actual merge. The Linux CI collector requires its success; failure,
cancellation, missing output or unexpected skipping cannot qualify. The legacy
`dev` required `verify` context collects the actual platform results. UI matrices
outside these profiles report not applicable, rather than pretending to execute.
Health retains source ownership/hygiene checks, without unrelated Rust or help
security scans blocking an isolated npm update.

Cargo, Actions and native binding updates retain complete acceptance. Main PRs,
merge groups, pushes, schedules, manual runs and release-source checks retain
full verification, apart from the separately qualified prose-only main PR rule.
The direct main/release check policy is unchanged. Do not classify by actor,
branch name, SemVer label or PR title alone. The existing real-Git scope controls
and CI policy fixtures own positive profiles, source/identity rejection and
failed/cancelled/missing selected-check evidence.

Dependency upgrades require manual reviewed PRs. The repository has no Dependabot
version-update configuration or dependency auto-merge workflow. GitHub's automated
security fixes setting must remain disabled independently of the removed version
configuration; verify it with `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/automated-security-fixes`.
Disabling PR generation must preserve Dependabot vulnerability alerts, dependency
review, CodeQL, secret scanning and their existing acceptance gates. Coverage
uploads requiring unavailable Dependabot credentials remain excluded; tests and
retained local artifacts are independent of external coverage publication.

The scheduled/manual glib migration watcher retains its resolution probe and
conditional build/test checks as advisory evidence with read-only repository
permissions. It never creates a dependency PR. Its all-resolved-branches migration
check remains authoritative; a successful probe does not authorize an upgrade or
claim native acceptance. Release maintenance retains its separately reviewed
next-development-version PR contract.

Deploy this policy through a reviewed main change, then align `dev` through a
reviewed integration. Existing `dev`
workflows cannot acquire fixes from main automatically. Preserve current required
checks; any protection migration uses its existing owner. Measure selected hosted
jobs after rollout, recording source, first failures, runner/setup/test time and
cache conditions. Local policy success is not a hosted latency or native claim.

Pinned native inspection downloads retain the exact version and SHA-256 owner in
`scripts/release/sevenzip.py`. Retryable transport failures may use the official
SourceForge distribution linked by the maintainer, within the same three-request
budget. Record bounded attempt/source/error diagnostics. Size, deadline, integrity,
installed-version and nonretryable HTTP failures remain fatal; never publish the
tool environment before successful verification. `release-sevenzip.test.mjs`
retains alternate-source, exhausted-budget and no-publication controls. Actual
installed-tool acceptance remains required on each consuming native platform.

### Synchronizing an accepted main source into dev

A pure main-to-dev synchronization introduces no product source beyond the exact
current main tip. The PR preparation owner may reuse the existing complete
trusted-main acceptance contract instead of retroactively applying the local
unit-only patch target to the entire development-branch backlog. This is limited
to `origin/dev` comparisons with a clean HEAD equal to the live remote main SHA.
`scripts/pr-platform/main-promotion.mjs` invokes the existing
`release/check-source-checks.mjs` owner: every required current-source check must
belong to its latest successful same-repository main-push workflow suite, with no
open main scanning alerts. PR-only, stale, pending, failed, skipped and wrong-suite
evidence cannot authorize promotion.

The verifier rechecks live main and local source after proof collection, bounds
network work and retires child processes through the existing process owner.
Failure, cancellation, changed source and unavailable evidence reject promotion.
This does not lower the configured patch target for ordinary new changes or
replace dev's current-head protected integration checks. Large ordinary diffs
remain fully measured within a bounded 32 MiB Git output budget; over-budget
input fails rather than becoming an empty or truncated patch.
"}

Linux union and real clean/use-after-free controls on all eight runners; a local
stable archive-protocol fixture does not qualify instrumentation or a cache hit.

work, on the hosted Linux runner. Apply this bound only at the compile step after
cache restoration to retain the compatible dependency cohort. The CLI rejects an
unbounded producer; consumer execution remains serial and every instrumentation
control and inventory requirement stays intact. Compare actual peak available
memory, swap and compilation time before revisiting this bound. Memory pressure
is an observed resource risk, not proof of an earlier runner-disconnection cause.
ASan compiles its core library once into an official Nextest archive, then runs
eight serial partitions. Runners 1–6 use Nextest `hash:ID/6`, excluding the
four exact reserved test names owned by `scripts/ci/asan.mjs`. Runner 7 executes

drift, duplicates and ignored cases. Preserve the complete strict union when
changing cohorts; compare actual instrumented timings before reconsidering them.
The producer seals the complete default inventory and
source/compiler/config/platform identity. Trusted job outputs bind both the
manifest and archive digests; consumers reject mismatches before extraction and
compare the extracted inventory before execution. Each runner retains the same
case budgets, instrumented standard library and real clean/error controls. The

archive transient and transfer it without another compression pass. Compare
producer compilation, artifact transfer, consumer preparation and queue time
alongside test execution; more shards alone can duplicate the dominant setup.
Keep extracted runtimes outside uploaded evidence. Collect receipts, inventories
and logs; do not upload another compiled binary copy from every consumer.
This separation also applies to failed or interrupted extraction. Use an owned
staging directory on the final target's filesystem, outside artifact roots, and
retire only that directory through the extraction owner's cleanup path. Exercise
rejection after real extraction and interrupted partial writes while preserving
unrelated native build outputs. Record image
rollout metadata separately from actual compiler/runtime compatibility; incidental
image version changes must not reject otherwise identical compatible inputs.
The ASan producer keeps bounded compile stdout/stderr and command lifecycle
receipts in a separate diagnostic artifact. Its resource observer samples fixed
kernel memory, swap, OOM and pressure counters, system load and workspace free
space every thirty seconds, at most 720 times. It retires its timer when work
settles, including cancellation; resource-observer read/write/live-output failures
never replace the compiler outcome or qualify an archive. Raw command receipts
retain the process owner's mandatory local write policy; receipt creation failure
rejects compilation admission. Only auxiliary upload transport is optional.

  assert.equal(process.platform, "linux", "Hosted ASan requires Linux");

  assert.match(sourceSha ?? "", /^[a-f0-9]{40}$/u, "ASan requires exact workflow source SHA");
  assert.match(runId ?? "", /^[1-9]\d*$/u, "ASan requires workflow run ID");
  assert.match(runAttempt ?? "", /^[1-9]\d*$/u, "ASan requires workflow run attempt");

  for (const value of [rustcSha256, cargoSha256]) assert.match(value ?? "", /^[a-f0-9]{64}$/u, "ASan requires cohort compiler fingerprints");

  for (const key of ["CARGO_ENCODED_RUSTFLAGS", "RUSTC_WRAPPER", "RUSTC_WORKSPACE_WRAPPER"]) assert.ok(!process.env[key], `ASan ${key} may override instrumentation`);

  const profileEnvironment = Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(process.env).filter(([key]) => key.startsWith("CARGO_PROFILE_")).sort(([a], [b]) => a.localeCompare(b)));
  const archive = process.env.MESH_ASAN_ARCHIVE_SHA256 || process.env.MESH_ASAN_MANIFEST_SHA256 ? { sha256: process.env.MESH_ASAN_ARCHIVE_SHA256, manifestSha256: process.env.MESH_ASAN_MANIFEST_SHA256 } : null;
  if (archive) for (const value of Object.values(archive)) assert.match(value ?? "", /^[a-f0-9]{64}$/u, "Missing trusted ASan build output digest");
  return { sourceSha, sourceTree, runId, runAttempt, platform: process.platform, architecture: process.arch, toolchain, rustcSha256, cargoSha256, nextest: versions.nextest, inputsSha256: digest(inputs), target, rustflags: process.env.RUSTFLAGS, rustdocflags: process.env.RUSTDOCFLAGS, asanOptions: process.env.ASAN_OPTIONS, testThreads: process.env.RUST_TEST_THREADS, profileEnvironment, archive };

Recommend **one bounded, same-source, whole Sanitizers workflow rerun**. Preserve attempt 1’s failure and require all eight shards plus strict union on the new attempt. No evidence currently justifies changing compiler jobs again, nightly, timeouts or instrumentation.

Evidence:

- [Current producer 134046431172](https://github.com/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/actions/runs/44085388181/job/134046431172) lost communication after compilation started at 12:42:39 UTC; job failed at 13:40:02. Its compile step remains `in_progress`; diagnostic/archive uploads never ran. This establishes runner loss, not OOM or compiler failure.
- Its only artifact reports storage preparation increased available space from **97,117,028,352 to 115,717,922,816 bytes**. That excludes initial disk shortage, not later exhaustion.
- **Updated finding:** [47bf run 44074522908](https://github.com/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/actions/runs/44074522908) completed successfully. Producer 134009491258, all eight shards and collector 134039126516 succeeded; collector logged **3,652 passed, 8 default ignored, 8 exact-source partitions** at 12:32:05 UTC.
- Both successful producer **133934049933** and successful 47bf producer **134009491258** used **Ubuntu 26.04 image 20261111.196.1**, provisioner 20261103.629. A checked 47bf consumer and collector used the same image.
- Current failed run’s **separate scope job** 134046343828 also used that image. The failed producer’s actual image remains unknown because its logs are unavailable; scope metadata cannot prove another VM’s image.
- No diff exists between 47bf and 257fd6ed in sanitizer workflow, ASan/shared command owners, `.cargo/config.toml`, root Cargo manifest or lockfile. Intervening changes concern docs and desktop notifications.

Image/cohort assessment:

GitHub confirms an active `ubuntu-latest` transition through November 19 and warns about system-library/prebuilt-binary compatibility. [Official rollout announcement](https://github.com/actions/runner-images/issues/14748). This creates an independent reproducibility risk, but successful producers already used Ubuntu26; rollback is **not an evidenced repair**. If explicitly pinning later, keep producer and every archive consumer on the same OS family and qualify the complete native instrumentation union. Current identity binds compiler/config/platform, **not OS ABI**.

Diagnostic/process review:

- Resource sampling is bounded: 30 seconds, at most 720 samples, bounded kernel reads and ≤8 KiB rows; it retires its timer and cannot change compilation success.
- Shared command termination targets its own detached child process group, not the hosted runner. No observed code path explains runner termination.
- Command output is capped at 128 MiB per channel; successful 47bf compile produced zero stdout and 10,367 stderr bytes. No evidence implicates diagnostic accumulation.
- Existing limitation remains: total VM loss defeats both live-log retention and subsequent artifact upload. Missing counters neither prove nor exclude memory starvation.

`docs/ci-maintenance.md:645` explicitly requires complete workflow recovery because archive/receipt identity includes `runAttempt`. If the bounded retry loses another runner without receipts, escalate the collected run/job/runner IDs to GitHub infrastructure support before speculative configuration changes.

name: Native core workflow evaluation

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      full:
        type: string
        default: 'true'
      upstream_result:
        type: string
        default: success
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  native:
    if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
    name: Real native UI (${{ matrix.os }})
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-24.04, windows-2022, macos-latest]
    runs-on: ${{ (inputs.full || 'true') == 'true' && matrix.os || 'ubuntu-latest' }}
    # Cold production/driver builds, native scenarios and evidence/cache cleanup
    # share this envelope. Keep the build and scenario watchdogs unchanged.
    timeout-minutes: 60
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 2
      - id: scope
        uses: ./.github/actions/ci-scope
        with:
          full: ${{ (inputs.full || 'true') }}
          upstream_result: ${{ inputs.upstream_result || 'success' }}
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: frontend/package-lock.json
      - name: Prepare hosted Linux build storage
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && (runner.os == 'Linux') }}
        id: runner_storage
        shell: bash
        run: sudo --preserve-env=GITHUB_ACTIONS,RUNNER_ENVIRONMENT,RUNNER_OS "$(command -v node)" scripts/ci/runner-storage.mjs --prepare | tee "$RUNNER_TEMP/runner-storage.json"

      - name: Preserve runner storage measurements
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && (always() && steps.runner_storage.outcome == 'success') }}
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: runner-storage-${{ github.job }}-${{ strategy.job-index || 0 }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/runner-storage.json
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 14

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        with:
          save-if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}
          # Keep compiled dependencies when a scenario fails, not its verdict.
          cache-on-failure: true
      - name: Diagnose multicast on the actual native test runner
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        run: node scripts/diagnostics/native-multicast-probe.mjs
      - name: Route the fixture multicast group locally (macOS runner only)
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && (runner.os == 'macOS') }}
        run: |
          sudo route -n add -host 224.0.0.167 -interface 127.0.0.1
          node scripts/diagnostics/native-multicast-probe.mjs --require
      - name: Prepare Ubuntu archive source
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && (runner.os == 'Linux') }}
        shell: bash
        run: sudo --preserve-env=GITHUB_ACTIONS,RUNNER_ENVIRONMENT,RUNNER_OS "$(command -v node)" scripts/ci/ubuntu-apt-source.mjs
      - name: Linux native webview dependencies
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && (runner.os == 'Linux') }}
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update --error-on=any
          sudo apt-get install -y libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev libayatana-appindicator3-dev librsvg2-dev patchelf libssl-dev xvfb openbox dbus-x11 xdotool fonts-noto-cjk fonts-noto-color-emoji
      - name: Install frontend dependencies
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        working-directory: frontend
        run: npm ci
      - name: Verify fail-closed evidence validator
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        run: node --test scripts/diagnostics/hidden-contacts-report.test.mjs scripts/diagnostics/png-evidence.test.mjs scripts/diagnostics/native-core-scenarios.test.mjs
      - name: Build source-pinned frontend, production app, CLI and native driver
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        run: node scripts/validation/native-build.mjs
      - name: Run native evaluation (Linux desktop session)
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && (runner.os == 'Linux') }}
        env:
          NATIVE_CONTACT_OUTPUT: ${{ runner.temp }}/hidden-contacts-native
          EVAL_SOURCE_SHA: ${{ github.sha }}
        run: |
          # Native focus and screenshot assertions require a real window manager.
          # shellcheck disable=SC2016
          xvfb-run -a -s '-screen 0 1600x1200x24' dbus-run-session -- bash -e -c '
            mkdir -p "$NATIVE_CONTACT_OUTPUT"
            openbox > "$NATIVE_CONTACT_OUTPUT/openbox.log" 2>&1 &
            node scripts/diagnostics/hidden-contacts.mjs
          '
      - name: Run native evaluation (Windows and macOS desktop)
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && (runner.os != 'Linux') }}
        env:
          NATIVE_CONTACT_OUTPUT: ${{ runner.temp }}/hidden-contacts-native
          EVAL_SOURCE_SHA: ${{ github.sha }}
        run: node scripts/diagnostics/hidden-contacts.mjs
      - name: Upload native evidence even on failure
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && (always()) }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: native-core-${{ matrix.os }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          # Publish evidence only, never fixture keystores or account data.
          path: |
            ${{ runner.temp }}/hidden-contacts-native/*.json
            ${{ runner.temp }}/hidden-contacts-native/*.png
            ${{ runner.temp }}/hidden-contacts-native/*.log
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 14

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      full:
        type: string
        default: 'true'
      upstream_result:
        type: string
        default: success
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  native:
    if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
    name: Real native UI (${{ matrix.os }})
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-24.04, windows-2022, macos-latest]
    runs-on: ${{ (inputs.full || 'true') == 'true' && matrix.os || 'ubuntu-latest' }}
    # Cold production/driver builds, native scenarios and evidence/cache cleanup
    # share this envelope. Keep the build and scenario watchdogs unchanged.
    timeout-minutes: 60
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 2
      - id: scope
        uses: ./.github/actions/ci-scope
        with:
          full: ${{ (inputs.full || 'true') }}
          upstream_result: ${{ inputs.upstream_result || 'success' }}
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: frontend/package-lock.json
      - name: Prepare hosted Linux build storage
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && (runner.os == 'Linux') }}
        id: runner_storage
        shell: bash
        run: sudo --preserve-env=GITHUB_ACTIONS,RUNNER_ENVIRONMENT,RUNNER_OS "$(command -v node)" scripts/ci/runner-storage.mjs --prepare | tee "$RUNNER_TEMP/runner-storage.json"

      - name: Preserve runner storage measurements
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && (always() && steps.runner_storage.outcome == 'success') }}
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: runner-storage-${{ github.job }}-${{ strategy.job-index || 0 }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/runner-storage.json
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 14

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        with:
          save-if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}
          # Keep compiled dependencies when a scenario fails, not its verdict.
          cache-on-failure: true
      - name: Diagnose multicast on the actual native test runner
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        run: node scripts/diagnostics/native-multicast-probe.mjs
      - name: Route the fixture multicast group locally (macOS runner only)
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && (runner.os == 'macOS') }}
        run: |
          sudo route -n add -host 224.0.0.167 -interface 127.0.0.1
          node scripts/diagnostics/native-multicast-probe.mjs --require
      - name: Prepare Ubuntu archive source
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && (runner.os == 'Linux') }}
        shell: bash
        run: sudo --preserve-env=GITHUB_ACTIONS,RUNNER_ENVIRONMENT,RUNNER_OS "$(command -v node)" scripts/ci/ubuntu-apt-source.mjs
      - name: Linux native webview dependencies
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && (runner.os == 'Linux') }}
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update --error-on=any
          sudo apt-get install -y libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev libayatana-appindicator3-dev librsvg2-dev patchelf libssl-dev xvfb openbox dbus-x11 xdotool fonts-noto-cjk fonts-noto-color-emoji
      - name: Install frontend dependencies
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        working-directory: frontend
        run: npm ci
      - name: Verify fail-closed evidence validator
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        run: node --test scripts/diagnostics/hidden-contacts-report.test.mjs scripts/diagnostics/png-evidence.test.mjs scripts/diagnostics/native-core-scenarios.test.mjs
      - name: Build source-pinned frontend, production app, CLI and native driver
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        run: node scripts/validation/native-build.mjs
      - name: Run native evaluation (Linux desktop session)
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && (runner.os == 'Linux') }}
        env:
          NATIVE_CONTACT_OUTPUT: ${{ runner.temp }}/hidden-contacts-native
          EVAL_SOURCE_SHA: ${{ github.sha }}
        run: |
          # Native focus and screenshot assertions require a real window manager.
          # shellcheck disable=SC2016
          xvfb-run -a -s '-screen 0 1600x1200x24' dbus-run-session -- bash -e -c '
            mkdir -p "$NATIVE_CONTACT_OUTPUT"
            openbox > "$NATIVE_CONTACT_OUTPUT/openbox.log" 2>&1 &
            node scripts/diagnostics/hidden-contacts.mjs
          '
      - name: Run native evaluation (Windows and macOS desktop)
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && (runner.os != 'Linux') }}
        env:
          NATIVE_CONTACT_OUTPUT: ${{ runner.temp }}/hidden-contacts-native
          EVAL_SOURCE_SHA: ${{ github.sha }}
        run: node scripts/diagnostics/hidden-contacts.mjs
      - name: Upload native evidence even on failure
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && (always()) }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: native-core-${{ matrix.os }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          # Publish evidence only, never fixture keystores or account data.
          path: |
            ${{ runner.temp }}/hidden-contacts-native/*.json
            ${{ runner.temp }}/hidden-contacts-native/*.png
            ${{ runner.temp }}/hidden-contacts-native/*.log
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 14
"}

**Keep ARM for this candidate. An Intel switch would change an explicit acceptance contract, not merely select an equivalent runner.**

The authoritative owners say:

- [testing-feedback-loop.md:245](/Users/kingsonwu/programming/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/.worktrees/asan-build-diagnostics-20261117/docs/testing-feedback-loop.md:245): “complete Rust workspace and real native desktop acceptance retain `macos-latest` Apple Silicon execution.”
- [ci-maintenance.md:578](/Users/kingsonwu/programming/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/.worktrees/asan-build-diagnostics-20261117/docs/ci-maintenance.md:578): ARM workspace and real native app/CLI checks retain `macos-latest`.
- [validation.json:520](/Users/kingsonwu/programming/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/.worktrees/asan-build-diagnostics-20261117/scripts/validation/validation.json:520) repeats that invariant and requires actual image labels in artifacts/collectors.

The current native harness is technically portable. `native-build.mjs` builds for its actual host without an ARM target override, records `process.arch`, and rejects build-proof architecture mismatches. `hidden-contacts-report.mjs` validates actual native Darwin behavior, source identity and every required scenario; it does not independently mandate ARM. That implementation flexibility does **not** override the maintained ARM contract.

**Correction to suspected Intel evidence:** jobs **134183442157** (`macOS native Host`) and **134183442413** (`macOS remaining archive`) both used `macos-latest`. The Host log confirms **macos-26-arm64 / 20261102.0473**, Node arm64 and `stable-aarch64-apple-darwin`. Host allocated successfully at **16:37:55**, near the native UI’s first allocation failure. This shows ARM allocation sometimes succeeds; it neither rules out pool pressure nor establishes a native UI defect.

GitHub explicitly documents macOS admission delays during high demand. `macos-26-intel` is a standard supported runner, with 4 Intel CPUs/14 GB RAM versus ARM’s 3 M1 CPUs/7 GB; availability and runtime are separate questions. [Official runner documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/runners/github-hosted-runners). Existing project measurements already warn that Intel browser qualification increased execution time; no comparable **native UI** Intel measurement establishes a benefit.

Retaining the literal required context while switching architecture is technically possible, but calling that unchanged acceptance would conceal the contract change. The context also feeds protected acceptance and exact-source release checks through [required-checks.mjs:12](/Users/kingsonwu/programming/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/.worktrees/asan-build-diagnostics-20261117/scripts/ci/required-checks.mjs:12); Host unit/coverage success does not replace real ARM GUI scenarios.

A future reviewed migration would need explicit acceptance redesign, synchronized workflow/docs/validation ownership, honest runner/artifact metadata, updated `ci-latency.test.mjs` and required-check tests, and fresh complete native Intel evidence. Preserving ARM GUI acceptance would still require an actual ARM execution owner.

For now: publish the corrected candidate, retain ARM, record these zero-step failures as infrastructure evidence, and use bounded recovery/escalation rather than changing architecture to clear the gate.
